extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, regulatory staff, OMB/OIRA personnel, and agency legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards set by Executive Order 13891 for how executive-branch agencies must define, publish, review, and issue guidance documents, including special rules for "significant" guidance and timelines for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance documents should be treated as non-binding both in law and in practice; agencies should take public input into account when appropriate and make guidance documents readily available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the order: "it is the policy of the executive branch, to the extent consistent with applicable law, to require that agencies treat guidance documents as non-binding both in law and in practice, except as incorporated into a contract, take public input into account when appropriate in formulating guidance documents, and make guidance documents readily available to the public." Also: "Agencies may impose legally binding requirements on the public only through regulations and on parties on a case-by-case basis through adjudications, and only after appropriate process, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract."

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'guidance document'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Guidance document" means an agency statement of general applicability, intended to have future effect on the behavior of regulated parties, that sets forth a policy on a statutory, regulatory, or technical issue, or an interpretation of a statute or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the explicit exclusions: (i) rules promulgated pursuant to notice and comment under section 553, (ii) rules exempt under 553(a), (iii) rules of agency organization/procedure/practice, (iv) decisions of agency adjudications under section 554, (v) internal guidance directed to the issuing agency not intended to have substantial future effect on regulated parties, and (vi) internal executive branch legal advice or legal opinions addressed to executive branch officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant guidance document criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A "significant guidance document" is one that may reasonably be anticipated to meet any of four listed impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order lists (i) annual effect on the economy of $100 million or more or material adverse effects on economy/sector/productivity/competition/jobs/environment/public health or on state/local/tribal governments or communities; (ii) create serious inconsistency or interfere with another agency's action; (iii) materially alter budgetary impact of entitlements/grants/user fees/loans or rights/obligations of recipients; (iv) raise novel legal or policy issues arising out of legal mandates, the President's priorities, or EO 12866 principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pre-enforcement ruling
rubrics_metrics.description: "Pre-enforcement ruling" means a formal written communication by an agency in response to an inquiry from a person concerning compliance that interprets or applies the law to facts supplied by the person, and includes informal guidance under SBREFA sec. 213, letter rulings, advisory opinions, and no-action letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single searchable guidance database requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of an OMB implementing memorandum, each agency must establish or maintain on its website a single, searchable, indexed database that contains or links to all guidance documents in effect from such agency or component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The website must note that guidance documents lack the force and effect of law, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract. Deadlines measured from the date on which OMB issues an implementing memorandum under section 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and rescission of existing guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 120 days of the OMB implementing memorandum, each agency shall review its guidance documents and, consistent with applicable law, rescind those guidance documents that it determines should no longer be in effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No agency shall retain in effect any guidance document without including it in the relevant database, nor shall any agency issue a guidance document without including it in the database. No agency may cite, use, or rely on guidance documents that are rescinded, except to establish historical facts. An agency may reinstate a rescinded guidance document within 240 days (from OMB memo date) without complying with procedures adopted under section 4, to the extent consistent with law, but must include it in the database.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Director waiver and reporting authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of OMB may waive compliance with database/review subsections for particular guidance documents or categories or extend deadlines; agency heads must report reasons for maintaining guidance documents when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may waive compliance with subsections (a) and (b) of section 3 for particular guidance documents or categories, or extend the deadlines. As requested by the Director, within 240 days of the OMB implementing memorandum, an agency head shall submit a report to the Director with the reasons for maintaining in effect any guidance documents identified by the Director. Reports will be provided to the President. The reporting subsection applies only to guidance documents existing as of the date of the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to promulgate agency procedures for issuing guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 300 days of the OMB implementing memorandum, each agency shall finalize regulations or amend existing regulations to set forth processes and procedures for issuing guidance documents consistent with this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The process set forth in each regulation shall be consistent with the order and include specific requirements (see separate criteria for required elements). Deadlines measured from the date on which OMB issues an implementing memorandum under section 6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statement that guidance does not bind the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Each guidance document must clearly state that it does not bind the public, except as authorized by law or as incorporated into a contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required element of the regulations agencies must adopt for issuing guidance documents (section 4(a)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for public petitions to withdraw or modify guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must include procedures for the public to petition for withdrawal or modification of a particular guidance document, including designation of the officials to which petitions should be directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required element of agency procedures for issuing guidance (section 4(a)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for significant guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For a significant guidance document, agencies must generally follow specified procedures unless the agency and the OMB Administrator agree exigency/safety/health/other compelling cause warrants an exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For significant guidance, required provisions include: (A) a period of public notice and comment of at least 30 days before issuance of a final guidance document, and a public response from the agency to major concerns raised in comments, except when the agency for good cause finds (and incorporates such finding and brief statement of reasons) that notice and comment are impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest; (B) approval on a non-delegable basis by the agency head or by an agency component head appointed by the President before issuance; (C) review by OIRA under Executive Order 12866 before issuance; and (D) compliance with the applicable requirements for regulations or rules, including significant regulatory actions, set forth in EOs 12866, 13563, 13609, 13771, and 13777.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator authority on exceptions and significance presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OMB Administrator shall issue memoranda establishing exceptions from the order for categories of guidance documents and categorical presumptions regarding whether guidance documents are significant, and may require submission of significant guidance to OIRA for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In light of a Memorandum of Agreement of April 11, 2018, sections on significance determinations and review shall not apply to the review relationship between OIRA and any component of the Department of the Treasury, or to compliance by the latter with the listed Executive Orders. Section 4(a)(iii) and section 5 shall not apply to pre-enforcement rulings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Executive Orders 12866/13563/13609
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements and procedures of Executive Orders 12866, 13563, and 13609 shall apply to guidance documents, consistent with section 4 of this order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 5: agencies must apply those EOs' requirements/procedures to guidance documents to the extent consistent with section 4.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB Director implementation authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall issue memoranda and, as appropriate, regulations pursuant to specified statutory authority to provide guidance regarding or otherwise implement the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6: Director to issue memoranda and regulations pursuant to sections 3504(d)(1) and 3516 of title 44, U.S.C., and other appropriate authority to implement this order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations, exceptions, and non-enforceability
rubrics_metrics.description: The order contains general provisions limiting its scope and effect, including non-impairment of statutory authority, subject to appropriations, not creating enforceable rights, and specified categories where the order does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 7 clarifies: (a) nothing in the order shall be construed to impair authority granted by law to departments/agencies or the Director of OMB functions; (b) implementation subject to applicable law and appropriations; (c) the order does not create any right or benefit enforceable at law or equity by any party; (d) exceptions include actions pertaining to foreign or military affairs or national security (with narrow procurement/import/export carve-out), criminal investigations/prosecutions, investigations of employee misconduct or disciplinary actions, documents exempt from disclosure under FOIA 552(b), and other circumstances where application would undermine national security as judged by agency head.
